resources.string: Find your misplaced phone with two consecutive hand claps
Microphone is inactive and consumes zero energy. Tap the button below to arm protection before locking your device.
Phone is listening for two rapid claps even while screen is off. Clap twice to locate your device.
Loud siren, flashing camera LED, and intense vibration active to guide you to your phone.
Persistent notification required to maintain microphone foreground service with instant stop action
Monitoring acoustic impulses for double claps. Tap to stop.
Alarm is currently ringing. Tap to silence audio and strobe.
Low (For noisy spaces to prevent false triggers)
High (For quiet spaces or muffled under blankets)
Blinks camera flash strobe to reveal device position in dark areas
Disables alarm automatically if three consecutive claps are heard without touching the device (Disabled by default)
This screen displays real-time input amplitude to help calibrate sensitivity. Audio is analyzed in volatile RAM and is never recorded or stored.
Try clapping twice with a 1-second gap to observe trigger behavior

1. Zero Audio Storage: Audio buffers (PCM 16-bit) are evaluated on-device in mathematical DSP loops and instantly discarded. Nothing is written to storage or network.

2. 100% Offline: No internet permission, zero telemetry, no cloud connectivity.

3. Partial WakeLock & Battery: A CPU wake lock keeps the audio pipeline running while the screen is off. Remember to disarm when not needed to conserve battery.

Important Note: In compliance with Android platform standards, this application cannot bypass Do Not Disturb (DND) or silent ringer volume without explicit system policy permissions. Please ensure your Alarm volume channel is audible.
Required solely for real-time acoustic clap detection while armed. No recordings are ever made or saved.
Required on Android 13+ to host the Foreground Service notification allowing screen-off monitoring.
